item.title: Bruno Fernandes misses Man U training ahead of Brentford clash
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes missed the club’s training session on Friday ahead of their Premier League meeting with Brentford on Saturday, raising concerns over his availability for the encounter. The Portuguese midfielder was absent from the session at Carrington after reportedly feeling slightly unwell. However, his absence was not linked to an injury, with the club opting to rest him as a precaution. According to ESPN, Fernandes is expected to recover in time for Saturday’s fixture at Old Trafford, with manager Mauricio Pochettino hopeful that the midfielder will be available for selection. Fernandes’ absence initially attracted attention after footage released by Manchester United from Friday’s training session showed the team preparing without their captain. The 32 year old remains an important figure in United’s midfield and has recorded six goal involvements in the Premier League this season, scoring four goals and providing two assists. He also comes into the Brentford encounter on the back of an impressive midweek performance, having scored twice in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw against his former club, Sporting. Pochettino will be looking to secure his first victory as United manager after the draw, having previously overseen encouraging performances against Liverpool and Sporting. Brentford, meanwhile, head to Old Trafford in confident mood after recording a convincing 4-0 victory over Everton last weekend. Their manager, Keith Andrews, has also expressed admiration for Pochettino, saying he had followed the Argentine’s teams during his own coaching career. Saturday’s meeting presents Pochettino with another opportunity to claim his first win as United manager, with Fernandes’ possible return expected to provide a significant boost to the hosts. item.title: A Trailblazing Woman In Engineering: Professor Patricia Onwuachi-Iheagwara Advances Nigeria’s Quest For Indigenous Oilfield Technology
item.description: From becoming Nigeria’s First Female Associate Professor of Petroleum Engineering in October 2021 to emerging as Nigeria’s First Female Professor of Petroleum Engineering in October 2024, her remarkable academic journey represents a milestone in engineering scholarship, gender advancement and indigenous technological innovation. In a landmark demonstration of academic distinction, professional excellence and commitment to indigenous technological development, Engr. Prof. Patricia Nneka Onwuachi-Iheagwara has delivered a compelling inaugural lecture at Southern Delta University (SDU), Ozoro, Delta State, calling for greater investment in home-grown research and technological solutions to strengthen Nigeria’s petroleum industry. The inaugural lecture, titled “From Earth to Wellbore: Confronting Cement Retrogression in HTHP Wells with Indigenous Additives,” delivered on 21 July 2026, brought into focus the importance of harnessing Nigeria’s natural resources and scientific capabilities to address critical engineering challenges confronting the oil and gas sector. Beyond its technical significance, the lecture represented another defining moment in the career of a distinguished academic whose professional journey has consistently challenged barriers in engineering education and research. Prof. Onwuachi-Iheagwara holds a remarkable place in Nigerian engineering history. In October 2021, she became Nigeria’s first female Associate Professor of Petroleum Engineering, establishing a significant national milestone in a specialised field traditionally dominated by men. In October 2024, she recorded another historic achievement as Nigeria’s first female Professor of Petroleum Engineering. Her subsequent emergence as the first female substantive Professor of Petroleum Engineering at Southern Delta University further reinforces her place among the pioneering women advancing engineering scholarship and professional excellence in Nigeria. A JOURNEY OF DISTINCTION AND HISTORIC ACHIEVEMENT Prof. Onwuachi-Iheagwara’s academic and professional development reflects an exceptional commitment to continuous learning, intellectual versatility and professional advancement. Her educational journey began with a Bachelor of Science degree in Geology from the University of Ilorin. She subsequently expanded her academic qualifications through postgraduate studies in Petroleum Engineering at the University of Benin, Mechanical Engineering at the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, and Petroleum Engineering at the University of Port Harcourt. She also obtained a Postgraduate Diploma in Education from Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, before completing her PhD in Petroleum Engineering at the University of Benin. Her professional experience before entering the academic environment cut across aviation, non-governmental organisations and computer programming for an indigenous oil servicing company. item.title: Ex-governor jailed 25 years for killing pregnant girlfriend
item.description: A former governor of Migori County in Kenya, Zacharia Okoth Obado, has been sentenced to 25 years in prison for his role in the 2018 murder of his pregnant girlfriend, Sharon Belyne Otieno. Obado was sentenced on Friday by Kenya’s High Court alongside two former aides who were convicted over the killing of the 26-year-old woman, who was seven months pregnant with his child at the time of her death. His former personal assistant, Michael Oyamo, was also handed a 25-year prison sentence, while former county clerk Caspal Ojwang’ Obiero received 18 years. The court found that Obado supplied the motive and financial resources for the murder, while Oyamo coordinated its execution. Obiero, on his part, was found to have provided logistical support and helped conceal the crime. According to the BBC, the court established that Obado was unhappy about the pregnancy resulting from his relationship with Otieno. Delivering the judgment, presiding judge Cecilia Githua said Obado’s absence from Migori when the murder occurred did not remove his responsibility for the crime. The judge rejected the prosecution’s request for the death penalty, as well as Obado’s plea for a non-custodial sentence. Otieno was abducted between September 3 and 4, 2018, shortly after leaving a hotel in Rongo, south-western Kenya, with journalist Barrack Oduor. She had reportedly contacted Oduor to discuss her relationship with Obado, who was then serving as governor. Oduor escaped from the abductors by jumping out of the moving vehicle, and his account later provided investigators with an important lead. Otieno’s body was subsequently found near Kodera Forest. A post-mortem examination established that she died from strangulation and excessive bleeding caused by multiple stab wounds. The court also confirmed that Obado was the biological father of her unborn child. Obado and the two former aides were convicted of murder on July 23, 2026, after prosecutors presented 42 witnesses and 81 exhibits during the trial. Before the sentencing, Otieno’s mother appealed to the court for leniency, describing Obado’s imprisonment as “another death in the family”. She urged the judge to consider a non-custodial sentence, arguing that Otieno’s three children from different relationships needed his support. However, Justice Githua maintained that the family’s circumstances could not take precedence over the court’s responsibility to impose an appropriate punishment. The court also declined to award compensation to Otieno’s family, citing insufficient evidence to establish the financial losses presented. Meanwhile, the family’s lawyer, Antony Opondo, told Kenya’s Daily Nation that they would appeal the decision, seeking Obado’s acquittal. The legal teams representing Obado and his co-defendants have also indicated plans to challenge their sentences. item.title: 2025 FGN-ASUU agreement: Ojukwu varsity threatens strike
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The state – owned Chukwuemeka Odumegwu Ojukwu University, COOU, branch of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, has threatened to embark on strike over non implementation of the 2025 agreement reached between the federal government and ASUU. Chairman of the institution’s ASUU, Comrade Bruno Ibekilo, at a press briefing by Owerri Zone of ASUU at Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Awka, described as unfortunate, the way the leadership of the university is handling the issue of the welfare of its members. “Presently, the university is not on strike, all in a bid to show commitment, but we have exhausted all means available to ensure industrial harmony while still pursuing the objectives we intend to achieve”, Ibekilo said. He said that although the state government has promised to start the implementation of the 2025 agreement in January 2027, the decision has not been communicated to the union officially. “By January 2027, if we don’t see the full implementation of the agreement, we will not have any other option than to down tools. If they want to implement the 2025 agreement, there must be a schedule for the payment of the arrears, which is now standing at one year. “By January, we will seek to get the arrears accompanying the agreement and other non financial components”, he said. Coordinator of ASUU Owerri Zone, Professor Dennis Aribodor, described non-payment of the withheld salaries as an undeserved punishment for academics, which, he observed, could snowball into a bigger crisis for the Nigerian university system. He lamented the lingering and unresolved issues affecting federal and state universities in ASUU Owerri Zone, recalling that since the twilight of the Buhari-led government, ASUU has continually demanded payment of the withheld salaries of its members in the wake of the 2022 nationwide strike occasioned by government’s failure to address issues arising from the poor implementation and non-renegotiation of the 2009 FGN-ASUU Agreement. He called on the Visitor to federal universities, President Bola Tinubu, to direct the immediate payment of three and half months salaries of ASUU members to deserving federal universities. Aribodor said: “Our members made enormous sacrifices to cover the lost grounds for the strike period to enable the affected students to graduate and move on with their lives. “At huge risks to their health, career progression and families, ASUU members forfeited their annual and research leaves, and doubled their efforts to regularise the academic calendar and stabilize the public university system. “The least expected of the Tinubu government is to direct the immediate release, the three and half months withheld salary of our members. item.title: Canada lists 28 African countries eligible for special study visa
item.description: Canada has listed 28 African countries whose citizens are eligible to apply for a special study permit programme that offers an opportunity to study in the country and potentially obtain permanent residence after graduation. The initiative, known as the Francophone Minority Communities Student Pilot (FMCSP), targets French-speaking international students seeking admission into selected Canadian post-secondary institutions outside Quebec. According to Canada’s immigration department, Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada (IRCC), the programme is designed to strengthen French-speaking minority communities by attracting international students who can contribute to their growth. The 28 eligible African countries are Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cabo Verde, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Comoros, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Republic of the Congo, Côte d’Ivoire, Djibouti, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Madagascar, Mali, Mauritania, Mauritius, Morocco, Niger, Rwanda, São Tomé and Príncipe, Senegal, Seychelles, Togo and Tunisia. Egypt is also eligible but is classified separately under the Middle East. To qualify, applicants must be citizens of one of the eligible countries, demonstrate French-language proficiency of at least level 5 on the NCLC scale in speaking, listening, reading and writing, and secure admission into a participating Canadian institution. They must also enrol in a full-time post-secondary programme lasting at least two years, leading to a diploma or degree, with more than 50 per cent of classes taught in French. Applicants must demonstrate sufficient funds to cover tuition, living expenses and transportation. The programme’s 2026–2027 intake opened on August 26, 2026, with a limit of 2,970 study permit applications until August 25, 2027. Among the participating institutions are the University of Ottawa, York University, Université de Moncton, Université de Saint-Boniface, Collège La Cité and Université Sainte-Anne. One of the major attractions is the opportunity for eligible graduates to apply for Canadian permanent residence. However, completing a programme does not automatically guarantee permanent residency, as applicants must meet additional immigration conditions. The permanent residence application pathway is scheduled to open in winter 2027. Nigeria is not among the 28 African countries eligible for the initiative. However, Nigerians can still apply for Canadian study permits through the regular international student route, subject to the country’s admission and immigration requirements. item.title: ‘Not a chance’ – Fulham coach Arbeloa rules out Calvin Bassey sale
item.description: Fulham manager Alvaro Arbeloa has ruled out the possibility of Nigeria international Calvin Bassey leaving the club during the January transfer window amid reported interest from Manchester United. Arbeloa described the 26-year-old defender as an important member of his squad, insisting that Fulham have no intention of allowing him to leave midway through the season. Manchester United are reportedly among several clubs monitoring Bassey following his impressive performances for the London club. However, speaking at his pre-match press conference ahead of Fulham’s meeting with Bournemouth, Arbeloa dismissed suggestions that the Red Devils could secure the defender’s services in January. “I’m so happy with Calvin,” Arbeloa told reporters at his pre-Bournemouth press conference. “Obviously, he’s not on sale. No chance that he can leave this club in January. I think he’s happy here, he’s one of our captains, he’s one of our leaders.” The Fulham manager also highlighted Bassey’s leadership qualities and importance to the team’s defensive setup, suggesting that his contributions extend beyond his performances on the pitch. Rather than being concerned about the reported interest from other clubs, Arbeloa views it as recognition of the defender’s performances and growing importance. Fulham are also understood to be taking steps towards securing Bassey’s long-term future, with discussions over a new contract already underway. The development could further complicate any potential attempt by Manchester United or other interested clubs to sign the Nigerian during the winter transfer window. Bassey has established himself as an important figure at Fulham since joining from Ajax in 2023, bringing defensive versatility, physical strength and experience to the squad. The former Rangers defender has also been a regular member of Nigeria’s national team, featuring prominently for the Super Eagles in international competitions. item.title: Meet Ime Udoka, Nigerian-American coach leading Houston Rockets in the NBA
item.description: Nigerian-American basketball coach Ime Udoka has built an impressive career in basketball, rising from representing Nigeria on the international stage to coaching some of the biggest teams in the National Basketball Association (NBA). Udoka, who currently serves as head coach of the Houston Rockets, has established himself as one of the prominent coaching figures in American basketball, with a career shaped by years of playing, coaching and leadership experience. Born on August 9, 1977, in Portland, Oregon, United States, Udoka has Nigerian roots and represented Nigeria in international basketball competitions before transitioning into coaching. His playing career included spells in the NBA, the NBA Development League and professional basketball leagues in Europe. He also played for Nigeria at the 2005 and 2011 FIBA AfroBasket tournaments, helping raise the country’s profile in international basketball. After retiring from professional basketball, Udoka moved into coaching, beginning his NBA coaching career as an assistant with the San Antonio Spurs in 2012. He worked under legendary coach Gregg Popovich, gaining experience in player development, team management and tactical preparation. During his time with San Antonio, the Spurs reached the NBA Finals in 2013 and won the championship in 2014, providing Udoka with valuable experience at the highest level of the sport. He subsequently served as an assistant coach with the Philadelphia 76ers and Brooklyn Nets before joining the Boston Celtics in 2021. Led Boston Celtics to NBA Finals Udoka’s breakthrough as a head coach came in 2021 when he was appointed to lead the Boston Celtics. In his first season, he guided the team to the 2022 NBA Finals, where they faced the Golden State Warriors. Although Boston lost the series 4-2, Udoka earned recognition for transforming the team’s defensive performance and guiding its players through a successful playoff campaign. His achievement made him one of the few coaches to reach the NBA Finals in his first season as a head coach. However, his tenure in Boston ended in September 2022 when the franchise suspended him for the 2022–23 season over violations of team policies. New chapter with Houston Rockets In April 2023, the Houston Rockets appointed Udoka as their head coach, giving him another opportunity to lead an NBA franchise. He took charge of a rebuilding team that had struggled in previous seasons and was tasked with improving its competitiveness through tactical discipline, player development and stronger defensive organisation. His appointment marked another significant milestone in his coaching career, as he became responsible for developing a young Houston squad and guiding the franchise towards sustained success. Udoka’s coaching approach has been associated with defensive intensity, accountability and high expectations for players. item.title: Nigeria’s future depends on mentally resilient youths — Mamora
item.description: Former minister urges graduates to embrace purpose, adaptability, continuous learning By Adeola Badru Former Minister of Health, Olorunnimbe Mamora, has said Nigeria’s future depends largely on the mental resilience, character development and sense of purpose of its youths, warning that academic qualifications alone are insufficient to prepare them for the challenges of the modern world. Mamora said young Nigerians must develop the capacity to navigate economic uncertainties, technological disruptions and changing employment opportunities through adaptability, continuous learning and problem-solving skills. He spoke while delivering the 18th Convocation Lecture of Ajayi Crowther University (ACU), Oyo, titled, “Youths’ Mental Health and Purpose: Thriving in a Volatile World.” The former minister challenged graduating students to look beyond the certificates they had earned and prepare for a world where success would increasingly depend on their ability to manage uncertainty, identify opportunities and remain relevant. He described convocation as a transition into a new phase of life, requiring graduates to demonstrate resilience, discipline, adaptability and a clear sense of purpose. Mamora identified the growing influence of social media, economic pressures and rapid technological advancement as emerging challenges to the mental wellbeing of young people. While acknowledging that the internet had expanded access to information and opportunities, he noted that excessive engagement with digital platforms could contribute to loneliness, anxiety and unhealthy comparisons. He urged graduates not to measure their achievements or personal worth against the lifestyles and apparent successes of others on social media. “Do not allow social media platforms to become the mirror through which you measure your worth. “Your value is not determined by the number of people who like your photograph. Stop comparing your backstage with somebody else’s stage,” he said. On the changing employment landscape, particularly with the emergence of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Mamora said graduates must recognise that education should go beyond acquiring academic qualifications. He stressed the importance of critical thinking, problem-solving, skills acquisition and continuous learning, noting that adaptability would be essential to remaining relevant in the evolving world of work. Drawing inspiration from the life of Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther, after whom the university was named, Mamora said the cleric’s journey from slavery to becoming a renowned missionary and scholar demonstrated the importance of determination and resilience in overcoming adversity. He urged the graduates to draw inspiration from Crowther’s life and remain committed to their aspirations despite the challenges they might encounter. item.title: Omo-Agege denies snubbing police invitation over Uduere killings
item.description: Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has denied reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. In a statement on Friday by his Media Adviser, Sunny Areh, the former Deputy President of the Senate said he had seen the reports and described them as untrue. “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege has seen the reports claiming he refused to honour an invitation from the Delta State Police Command over Monday’s attack on members of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, at Uduere. “It isn’t true. You can’t turn down an invitation you never received,” he said. According to the statement, no formal invitation has reached the Senator or his office. “No letter has reached the Senator or his office, and no officer has come to him with one. He first learned of it the same way everyone else did, from the Command’s announcement in the media.” Areh said the report that Omo-Agege refused to appear was based on a single unnamed source. “The claim that he refused leans on a single unnamed source. The Senator hasn’t told the police, or anyone else, that he won’t appear.” The statement also revisited the events at Uduere, insisting that Omo-Agege was the victim of the attack. “It is worth remembering what happened at Uduere. Senator Omo-Agege was the target of an assassination attempt. Senior members of his campaign team were murdered, and others are still in hospital with serious injuries. “He is the one who survived an attack on his life, and the one demanding that those responsible be found and prosecuted.” Omo-Agege said he wants the case resolved and justice for the victims. “He wants this case resolved, and he wants justice for the dead and the wounded. If the police serve a lawful invitation, he will honour it. He asks only that it be sent through his office so a date can be agreed.” He faulted the manner in which the alleged invitation was made public. “A summons announced in the press before it reaches the person named is not due process, and he won’t be tried in the media,” he said. item.title: 2027: National Counter Terrorism Centre moves to foil attacks on INEC facilities, personnel
item.description: ..Laka warns against electoral violence, voter intimidation, destruction of infrastructure By Kingsley Omonobi The National Counter Terrorism Centre (NCTC), Office of the National Security Adviser, has said it is working with security agencies to prevent planned attacks on Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) offices, personnel and electoral infrastructure ahead of the 2027 general elections. The National Coordinator of the Centre, Major General Adamu Laka, also said measures were being strengthened to protect voters and prevent emerging security threats from disrupting the electoral process. Laka spoke at the National Flag-off/North Central Zone Town Hall Engagement on Preventing Electoral Violence and Strengthening Election Security in Nigeria. He urged youths not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence, describing them as critical stakeholders in the country’s democratic future. “In this regard, I urge our young people not to allow themselves to be used as instruments of political violence. You are important stakeholders in Nigeria’s democratic future and your energy, creativity and influence should be directed towards promoting peace, tolerance and responsible civic participation,” he said. He said the Centre was working towards preventing attacks on INEC offices and personnel, protecting voters and electoral infrastructure, countering fake news and inflammatory narratives, strengthening community-based early warning systems and ensuring timely responses to emerging security threats. Describing elections as the heartbeat of democracy, Laka said their credibility depended not only on the conduct of voting and announcement of results but also on the peace, security and public confidence surrounding the entire electoral process. “There is absolutely no gain in any loss of life or property as a result of this democratic process,” he said. The NCTC coordinator identified misinformation and disinformation, hate speech, political intolerance, incitement, youth manipulation, political thuggery, vote buying, voter intimidation, voter suppression and destruction of public infrastructure as factors that could fuel electoral violence. He said stakeholders must collectively address the threats and strengthen early warning and response mechanisms to identify potential dangers before they escalate into violence. Laka also stressed the need to build public confidence in the electoral process and ensure that women, youths, persons with disabilities and internally displaced persons were not excluded from meaningful participation. He maintained that preventing electoral violence was not the responsibility of security agencies alone but required the collective commitment of political actors, government institutions, traditional and religious leaders, civil society organisations, the media and community-based organisations. item.title: OK Movement withdraws support for Obi, Kwankwaso, NDC

item.title: ADC waste plan will create 21,000 jobs in Lagos – Gbadamosi
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye African Democratic Congress (ADC) deputy governorship candidate Babatunde Olalere Gbadamosi has projected that the party’s waste management plan would create at least 21,000 jobs in Lagos, including 20,000 for waste collection crews. Gbadamosi, who is running with ADC governorship candidate Gbadebo Rhodes-Vivour, spoke at the Road to Election 2027 Lagos Deputy Governorship Debate on Nigeria Info FM on Friday, where he outlined proposals on employment, waste collection, housing and transportation. Addressing unemployment, Gbadamosi said he did not know the state’s unemployment rate and disputed figures published by the Lagos government. He proposed a review of public sector salaries and said his plans for waste management, housing, transportation and education would create jobs for Lagosians. “First of all, the truth is, I suppose the truth is, I really don’t know what the unemployment rate is. Whatever figures that are put out by the APC government of Lagos State are usually just false. They just manufacture figures, yank them out of their a**,” he said. He said he and Rhodes-Vivour had agreed to “undertake a review, a wholesale review of public sector salaries, in order to bring them in line with our current economic realities.” He also cited plans for 20,000 jobs in waste-to-energy, 100,000 affordable housing units and 16,000 electric buses. “We plan to bring 16,000 electric buses into Lagos State because we simply don’t have enough capacity to carry the 24 million people of Lagos State on the current transportation system,” he said, adding that the housing and transport plans would also provide work for young people. On waste collection, Gbadamosi proposed providing each local government with at least 200 dumpsters. He estimated that 4,000 trucks, each with a five-person crew, would create 20,000 jobs. “All right, we have 20 local governments. So 200 times 20, that’s 4000 trucks. 4000 trucks times five crew members, each. That’s already 20,000 jobs,” he said. He estimated that recycling centres would create at least another 1,000 jobs, based on a minimum of 50 workers at each of 20 local government centres. “That’s 50 jobs times 20 local governments. That’s already what 1000 extra jobs minimum,” he said, adding that the programme would be funded with “25% of Lagos State revenue that is being paid to Alpha Beta at the moment.” Other major contenders at the debate included Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) deputy governorship candidate Moriam Tolani Animashaun and Social Democratic Party (SDP) deputy candidate Kayode Evelyn Aderiyike. item.title: PANDEF rejects 20% NCDMB fund deduction for research council
item.description: …Warns against diversion of local content funds, urges NASS to review proposed legislation By Henry Umoru ABUJA – The Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF), the apex socio-political body of the South-South geopolitical zone, has rejected the proposed 20 per cent deduction from the Nigerian Content Development Fund to finance the proposed National Council on Research, Science, Technology and Innovation. The forum warned that the move could undermine years of investment in indigenous industrial capacity and weaken the Nigerian Content Development and Monitoring Board (NCDMB), which has been instrumental in promoting local expertise, skills acquisition, enterprise development and industrialisation. PANDEF urged the National Assembly to review Section 19 of the proposed legislation establishing the council and reject the provision earmarking 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund for its financing. Addressing journalists in Abuja on Friday, PANDEF National Chairman, Ambassador Godknows Igali, acknowledged the Federal Government’s efforts to strengthen the country’s research, science, technology and innovation capacity but expressed concern over Part IV, Section 19(a) of the proposed Bill. He described the proposed funding arrangement as inappropriate, counterproductive and fundamentally flawed, arguing that a new national institution should not be financed by weakening an existing statutory agency with clearly defined responsibilities and ongoing development commitments. Igali said the NCDMB, which commenced operations in 2010, had a statutory mandate to promote the development, acquisition and application of indigenous capacity in Nigeria’s oil and gas industry. He noted that the Nigerian Content Development Fund was already supporting strategic investments in the oil and gas sector and related areas, including agriculture, manufacturing and transportation. According to him, diverting 20 per cent of the fund could disrupt existing commitments, constrain ongoing investments and slow the progress recorded in local content development. “The Nigerian Content Development Fund is not an idle pool of resources awaiting allocation. It is an active development instrument that is already financing and supporting several strategic investments in the oil and gas industry and related sectors of the Nigerian economy,” he said. Igali also warned that the proposed funding mechanism could establish a dangerous precedent in public finance, whereby newly established government institutions would depend on deductions from funds already allocated to existing statutory agencies. item.title: Photos: Adeleke sworn in for 2nd term; says ‘Let’s heal our past wounds’
item.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo As Governor Ademola Adeleke took oath of office for his second term tenure, he has charged the Osun State political class to allow the wounds of the past to heal and collaborate to develop the state. Governor Adeleke spoke while addressing hundreds of dignitaries and residents who thronged the Osogbo township stadium to be part of his inauguration. He disclosed that citizens, irrespective of political affiliations, must unite for the collective good. His words: “Fellow citizens, we must heal the wounds of the past and unite for our collective good. I charge the Osun political class to embrace elite consensus, transparency, good governance and local content”. The governor commended the resilience of the citizens and residents of the state to safeguard democracy, saying their commitment has become a national model. “Today is a triumph of the people’s will. I give all glory to God and deeply thank the people of Osun. Their commitment to democracy is today a national model,” he said. 2nd term focus On his administration’s focus for the second term, he said the target of the government will focus on citizens’ welfare, infrastructure expansion, industrialisation, agricultural transformation, digital economy, tourism industry, wealth creation, and youth and women’s development among others. “As growth depends on steady power supply, we will immediately set up the Osun State Electricity Regulatory Commission. This is in line with the power sector law I signed earlier this year. “Job and Wealth creation will be at the heart of our second term. We will establish a digital hub in each of our three senatorial districts. This is to drive job creation in the digital economy. “In education, we will recruit more teachers and speed up school rehabilitation. We will expand bursaries and scholarships, keep tuition affordable, tackle cultism, and revive our technical colleges.” Osun local government crisis On the issue of local government crisis, Adeleke said: “I am glad to announce that Mr President has intervened in the local government matter. In the next one week, the crisis will be fully resolved. Once this is done, our administration will ensure the rehabilitation of the remaining 102 primary health care centres.” Earlier, the deputy governor, Kola Adewusi took oath of office at 11:24a.m. followed by that of the governor whose oath of office was administered by the Chief Judge, Justice Oyebola Adepele-Ojo at exactly 11:34am. item.title: [PHOTOS] Adeleke Sworn In For Second Term As Osun Governor
item.description: Osun State Governor, Ademola Adeleke, has been sworn in for a second term, beginning another four-year tenure that will run until 2030. Adeleke took the oath of office on Friday, November 27, 2026, at an inauguration ceremony held at the Osogbo Township Stadium. The state Chief Judge administered the oath of office to Deputy Governor Kola Adewusi before swearing in Adeleke. The ceremony was attended by Vice President Kashim Shettima, who led several dignitaries, including former Osun State Governor Bisi Akande, Ondo State Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa, and former Senate President Bukola Saraki. The entertainment industry was also represented, with Afrobeats singer Davido, alongside B-Red and Shina Rambo, attending the ceremony to celebrate the governor. Adeleke secured re-election in the August 15, 2026 governorship election on the platform of the Accord Party after defecting from the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). He polled 511,067 votes to defeat the All Progressives Congress (APC) candidate, Bola Oyebamiji, who secured 444,815 votes. Osun Governor Ademola Adeleke sworn in as governor for a second term. item.title: Full list: African countries where travelers can access without visa
item.description: Travelling across Africa is becoming easier as more countries adopt visa-free entry policies aimed at promoting tourism, strengthening regional integration and encouraging trade among African nations. Several African countries have introduced policies allowing citizens of other African countries to visit without obtaining a visa before travelling, reducing the cost and administrative hurdles associated with cross-border movement. Among the countries offering such access are Benin, The Gambia, Rwanda, Seychelles, Ghana and Togo. The policies form part of wider efforts to improve freedom of movement across the continent and advance the African Union’s goal of greater economic integration. The six countries are highlighted below, although their entry arrangements are not identical. 1. Benin Benin is one of Africa’s leading supporters of visa-free movement. It allows citizens of other African countries to enter without obtaining a visa before travelling. The country has promoted easier cross-border movement to encourage tourism, business and regional cooperation. 2. The Gambia The Gambia offers visa-free entry to citizens of other African countries. It is one of the continent’s more open destinations, making it attractive to visitors interested in tourism, business and cultural exchanges. 3. Rwanda Rwanda allows citizens of African Union member states to enter without a visa. The policy supports the country’s efforts to attract African visitors, investors and business travellers. 4. Seychelles Seychelles operates a visa-free entry policy for visitors of all nationalities, including African travellers. However, visitors must obtain the required travel authorisation before departure and meet the country’s entry conditions. 5. Ghana Ghana introduced a free visa policy for African nationals in May 2026. Under the arrangement, African travellers can apply for electronic visas without paying visa fees. However, an application and approval are still required, meaning the policy is not strictly visa-free entry. 6. Togo Togo has introduced visa-free entry for African passport holders, subject to pre-arrival requirements. The policy is part of efforts to facilitate movement across the continent and strengthen regional integration. item.title: Kano govt to Kwankwaso: Stop dragging Yusuf into EFCC troubles
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government has asked former Governor Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso to stop linking Governor Abba Kabir Yusuf to his alleged dealings with the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC). The government said Yusuf had no involvement in Kwankwaso’s issues with the anti-graft agency, which it claimed predated the current administration. The Commissioner for Information and Internal Affairs, Sunusi Bature Dawakin Tofa, stated this in a statement issued on Friday. He described Kwankwaso’s allegations against the governor as misleading and politically motivated. According to the government, it was wrong for the former governor to accuse Yusuf of influencing the EFCC investigation when the matter began before his administration. “The crisis and court cases involving the NDC are internal party matters arising from disagreements among its members, and the Kano State Government has no involvement in them,” the statement said. The government accused Kwankwaso of using the governor as a target to gain public sympathy and remain politically relevant ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Rather than constantly blaming the Kano State Government for his political difficulties, Kwankwaso should concentrate on resolving the internal challenges confronting his political camp,” the statement said. It maintained that Yusuf was elected to govern Kano State and deliver development, not to engage in political arguments or take responsibility for the problems of other political parties. The government urged Kwankwaso to allow the administration to focus on fulfilling its promises to the people, warning that attempts to gain public sympathy through political blackmail would not succeed. “You cannot win public sympathy through blackmail and unfounded allegations,” it said. The statement added that the people of Kano State would have the opportunity to judge political leaders through their votes in 2027. It further reaffirmed that Yusuf remained committed to governance, development and the welfare of residents. Recall that Kwankwaso had accused Governor Yusuf of using the EFCC and other government institutions to target him and members of his family for political reasons ahead of the 2027 elections. He also alleged that the governor attempted to pressure the EFCC through protests at its office and interfere in a case involving the NDC governorship candidate. item.title: Arsenic In The Water: Thailand Presses Myanmar Over Mining Pollution
item.description: As pollution mounts in its rivers, food and water, Thailand is pressing neighbouring Myanmar to tackle unregulated mining, while urging China to exert its influence in the war-ravaged nation. Tap water supplies to 14 villages in Mae Sai district near the Myanmar border were suspended earlier this month after arsenic levels were found to be nearly 30 times government limits. Bangkok this week hosted the first Thai-Myanmar working group on the issue — also attended by the Chinese ambassador — where it said tests proved rare-earth and gold mines in Myanmar were causing the pollution downstream. The two sides agreed to joint water sampling on the Kok and Sai rivers. This photo taken on June 5, 2026 shows Wan Wiriya, assistant professor from Chiang Mai University, showing the results of an arsenic level test from a water sample (C) taken from the Kok River, next to a control sample of drinking water (R) near the the northern Thai city of Chiang Rai. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP But there was no public agreement to Thailand’s request for a six-month suspension of operations, and how one could be implemented remains unclear, with Myanmar’s military not in full control. Bangkok is also looking to China, the main importer of rare-earth materials from Myanmar, to pressure private Chinese operators, as a months-long concern becomes increasingly urgent. Authorities warned residents this week against eating certain shellfish and other river species after tests in northern and northeastern Thailand found dangerous levels of arsenic and lead. Saengwaree Suvirakan, a farmer from Tha Ton in Chiang Mai province who joined a protest in Bangkok this week, said fish stocks were declining in any case. “Now with the mines the fish are all gone,” she said. ‘Not from nature’ This photo taken on June 4, 2026 shows fishermen and their boats near the confluence of the Kok River and Mekong River in Chiang Saen, northern Thailand’s Chiang Rai province. Photo by LILLIAN SUWANRUMPHA / AFP At the joint talks, Thai ministers said high arsenic levels in the Kok and Sai rivers could only have come from rare-earth and gold mines on the Myanmar side. “Arsenic does not come from nature, it came from mining sites. The source was from (Myanmar’s) Shan state, no-one disagrees,” Science Minister Yodchanan Wongsawat said. But how to tackle it remains an issue. Thanapon Piman, senior research fellow at the Stockholm Environment Institute (SEI), welcomed the agreement on joint sampling sites. “This is going to be a first step to agree on the evidence, otherwise you cannot move to the next step, like stopping mining activity,” he told AFP. But Myanmar intervening to stop mining would be “really difficult”, he added. Multiple ethnic armed groups have been operating there for decades, while a 2021 military coup sparked an ongoing civil war.
